newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev edges up as dlr shortcovering eases.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev edges up as dlr shortcovering eases.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev firmed to 1,517-1,520 to dollar at close from the morning's 1,518-1,522 as foreign currency shortcovering eased on the interbank market, dealers said.

"Demand for dollars subsided a bit in the afternoon and the lev edged up from the morning lows. But the lev is still softer from yesterday because large clients like fuel importers bid for dollars, keeping pressure on the lev," a bank dealer said.
The lev closed at around 1,507-1,509 per dollar on Tuesday.

Today's foreign currency demand came mainly from banks and clients which have pared forex positions in the past several days to invest in government securities but have failed to place winning bids at the auctions, traders said.
(Those investors) today were buying back the foreign currency they sold for levs in the hope of locking them in treasury paper," another dealer said.

Floating interest T-bill issues with maturities of six, nine and 12 months offered at Monday's auctions were heavily subscribed but the Finance ministry rejected around two thirds of the bids, seeking a higher average accepted price.
